# RandomRotation — rotating every wheel at random

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean · **Diagram:** [Foundations: wheels, cycles and columns](../../GRAPH.md#foundations-wheels-cycles-and-columns)

Turn each wheel to a position chosen uniformly at random, independently. The chance that every member of a given finite set of positions survives equals the product over the wheels of one minus the number of distinct positions the set occupies on that wheel over the wheel size: exactly the pattern's survivor share. By the Chinese Remainder Theorem each choice of rotations is a shift of the whole cycle, so this is a count of shifts. The random-sieve model of Banks, Ford and Tao and the starting point of the large-gap construction (Ford Lemma 8.4). As proved: matches the plan; the survival share is stated for the wheels below the limit, as the share of the cycle surviving the pattern.

**What it adds:** SurvivorCount counts the surviving positions of the cycle; this node reads that count as a probability: each setting of the wheels is one shift of the cycle (CRT), so the survival chance under random rotations is the pattern's survivor share.

## Claims

<a id="rotation_is_shift"></a>
### `rotation_is_shift`

Every choice of one position per active wheel is exactly one position of the combined cycle.

```lean
/-- **A setting of the wheels is a shift of the cycle.** For every choice of
a position on each active wheel there is exactly one position of the combined
cycle reading as that choice. -/
def rotation_is_shift : Prop :=
  ∀ (limit : Nat) (s : ∀ q : active_primes limit, ZMod (q : Nat)),
    ∃! n : ZMod (primorial_modulus limit), crt_map limit n = s
```

**Rests on:** [`CRT.crt_map_bijective`](CRT.md#crt_map_bijective)

**Proof:** `RNS.RandomRotation.rotation_is_shift_step` in [`RNSSolutions/RandomRotation.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/RandomRotation.lean)

<a id="random_rotation_survival"></a>
### `random_rotation_survival`

Under random rotations the chance that a pattern survives is the product over the wheels of one minus w over the wheel size.

```lean
/-- **The survival chance under random rotations.** The shifts of the cycle
under which every member of the pattern `T` survives every active wheel, as a
share of the cycle length, equal the product over the active wheels of one
minus `w T q` over `q`. -/
def random_rotation_survival : Prop :=
  ∀ (T : Finset Nat) (limit : Nat),
    ((wheel_survivors_gen T limit).card : ℝ) / (primorial_modulus limit : ℝ) =
      ∏ q ∈ active_primes limit, (1 - (w T q : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))
```

**Rests on:** [`SurvivorCount.general_survivor_count`](SurvivorCount.md#general_survivor_count)

**Proof:** `RNS.RandomRotation.random_rotation_survival_step` in [`RNSSolutions/RandomRotation.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/RandomRotation.lean)
